translations.answer: The maintainer's direct reason is: when a real-time thread holds the publish lock while non-realtime threads are blocked, the real-time thread's subsequent unlock is no longer a real-time safe operation. The original author used comments on `unlockAndPublish()` and RTAI syscall number to perform A/B localization. The project claims the default branch is fixed, but no commit or release version is provided, so the conclusion can only be used to identify this lock contention pattern.
translations.applicability: Directly applicable to the old RealtimePublisher/RTAI implementation; current version requires re-measurement.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: A/B comments on `unlockAndPublish()` and confirm with RTAI/dmesg syscall numbers.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Restart or reinsert RTAI module, check dmesg for first hard-to-soft syscall; original author confirmed the machine is 32-bit, so 240 corresponds to futex.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: The maintainer claims the default branch fixed the lock contention path.
translations.details.environments.0: 2012 ros_control; 32-bit RTAI user-space real-time loop; specific commit not given.
translations.details.limits.0: Conclusion is bound to the old ros_control/RTAI implementation; cannot infer modern `realtime_tools` internal implementation from this thread.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Root cause is explicitly stated by the maintainer; the thread does not provide syscall count, commit, or release after fix.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does `RealtimePublisher::unlockAndPublish()` trigger a futex system call on a real-time thread?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: WBC real-time publish path should be tested for lock contention pressure on the target kernel, not just in conditions with no subscribers or low load.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The maintainer confirmed: real-time thread holds the lock while non-realtime threads begin to block; after that, the real-time thread's unlock enters a non-realtime safe path.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Calling `unlockAndPublish()` results in `LXRT CHANGED MODE (SYSCALL)` with syscall number 240; commenting on the call prevents this.
translations.source.locator: ros_control #8 syscall observation 10822469; maintainer root cause and fix explanation 13088686
translations.source.title: RealtimePublisher Unlocking Causes Non-Realtime Waiters to Disrupt Realtime Safety
translations.terms.2: Fast user-space mutex (futex) (快速用户态互斥锁)
translations.title: Why does the old ros_control's `unlockAndPublish()` cause a futex system call in the real-time loop?
